messages:
marco: Heads-up - customer on a serverless deploy saw duplicate side-effects from onboarding sample when a 429 and token refresh coincided, but duplicates persisted across cold restarts.
lena: oof, that sounds like the usual immediate-replay problem + no durable idempotency. cold starts break any in-memory auto-key approach.
ravi: can you share the timeline? curious about Retry-After handling too.
marco: sanitized trace:
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z auth: refresh:start
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z api: 429 route=/v1/issueInvoice
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z auth: refresh:done
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z client: replaying original request (no idempotency key)
--- process crash/hot restart ~50ms later ---
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z client restarted
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z client: replaying original request again (no persisted key)
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z api: invoice created id=inv_01
2026-04-10T02:12:10Z api: invoice created id=inv_02
marco: two creates ~100ms apart but across a restart; in-memory fixes wouldn't help.
lena: ah, serverless cold restarts are exactly why we can't rely on ephemeral keys. We should show an outbox/durable idempotency pattern in the onboarding sample.
ravi: agree. Options: 1) outbox (write intent + durable idempotency key persisted to disk or small local DB before calling API), 2) require caller-provided idempotency keys in production, 3) SDK-provided optional file-backed key store for durability.
infra: also check Retry-After header parsing. If server returned Retry-After we should honor it rather than immediate replay. Did this request include Retry-After?
marco: in this case server didn't return Retry-After, just 429. SDK sample currently does immediate replay after refresh.
lena: propose sampleapp change: implement a minimal outbox example using SQLite or a small file store. Show pattern: 1) create idempotency key, persist (outbox), 2) attempt request, 3) on success remove outbox entry, 4) on process restart, background worker flushes outbox. This handles restarts.
ravi: sample snippet (Node-ish):
```
// simple file-backed outbox example
const id = uuidv4()
await outbox.store({idempotencyKey: id, payload})
try {
  const res = await client.post('/v1/create', payload, {headers: {'Idempotency-Key': id}})
  await outbox.remove(id)
} catch (err) {
  // leave entry; background flush will retry respecting Retry-After or jitter
}
```
Add note: flush worker should honor Retry-After and apply jitter/exponential backoff.
marco: exactly. That would avoid duplicates across restarts.
lena: SDK-level suggestion: offer an optional durable idempotency helper exposing a pluggable store interface (memory, sqlite, redis). Something like `sdk.idempotency.store = new FileStore(path)` and a helper `sdk.idempotency.wrapSend(fn, opts)` that manages the write-ahead pattern.
ravi: also SDK should parse Retry-After (both seconds and HTTP-date), and when not present fall back to reasonable jitter+backoff. Don't ignore Retry-After or you risk thundering.
infra: agree. Also add a telemetry tag `durable_outbox_used=true` when outbox helper is active so SRE can see adoption.
marco: QA: add an e2e that simulates 429+refresh + process restart and assert single side-effect when using outbox pattern. qa-bot: created test card DX-378123 "durable-outbox onboarding test" with steps and expected results. :white_check_mark:
qa-bot: test card linked to sampleapp PR when ready.
lena: docs: add a "Serverless & cold-starts" section explaining why in-memory idempotency can fail and show the outbox pattern. Also include a checklist: prefer caller-supplied durable idempotency keys, if not possible use SDK file-backed store or Redis.
ravi: one caveat: storing keys client-side may have compliance implications (PII/PHI) depending on payload. Document guidance: persist only idempotency metadata (key, endpoint, timestamp) not full payload unless customer opts in and is aware.
marco: good call. We'll redact payload in examples and warn about storing sensitive data.
lena: timeline: I'll draft sampleapp outbox example + docs this sprint. Ravi will prototype SDK `idempotency.store` helper next sprint (opt-in behind flag). Infra will evaluate a Redis example for heavy-duty apps.
infra: will also check whether we can emit a server-side small dedupe window as complementary protection but not rely on it.
ravi: tests: unit tests for store interface, e2e with simulated restart, and telemetry events for outbox usage.
marco: any objections? or other ideas?
lena: no objections. this is different enough from jitter-only fixes and covers serverless cases. :thumbsup: 
qa-bot: noted - will watch PRs and run DX-378123 when ready.
marco: thanks all, i'll open sampleapp PR with the outbox pattern and link the QA card.
